title: Amazing Animal Stories!
summary: Josh and Chuck present three "amazing animal" stories. First, Mike the Headless Chicken: Lloyd and Clara Olsen's rooster survived decapitation on their Colorado farm, was taken up by sideshow promoter Hope Wade, toured the country, and lived about eighteen months without a head before choking on corn after the syringe used to clear its esophagus was left behind. Second, Voytech the Bear: a Syrian brown bear cub adopted by the Polish Second Corps artillery unit in Iran, who came along to Egypt and Italy (Monte Cassino), was given rank as a private, and after the war lived in Scotland and at the Edinburgh Zoo until dying in 1963. Third, Bumps the St. Bernard: adopted by the Royal Norwegian Navy during World War Two alongside Lieutenant Erling Haftorn, who served on the whale-catcher-turned-patrol boat Thorodd, was known for bravery, rescues and bus-riding, and received a posthumous PDSA Gold Medal in 2006. The episode closes with a listener mail about the MH370 episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and Mike the Headless Chicken
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about animals, a playground anecdote, and then tell the story of Mike the Headless Chicken, whose head was cut off on the Olsen farm near Fruita, Colorado, and who lived on after being toured by sideshow promoter Hope Wade.

segments.title: Mike the Headless Chicken story
segments.summary: Lloyd Olsen accidentally beheaded a rooster but it survived. Hope Wade took the Olsens and Mike on tour, scientists in Salt Lake City examined him, Life Magazine covered him, and he earned large sums. The brain stem survived, and the Olsens fed him with an eyedropper. Mike died of choking on corn in Arizona after the syringe was left behind.

segments.title: Voytech the Bear and the Polish Second Corps
segments.summary: Polish soldiers in Iran in World War Two acquired a Syrian brown bear cub, adopted it as a unit mascot and private, took it to Egypt and Italy where it carried artillery shells at Monte Cassino, and after the war it lived in Scotland and at the Edinburgh Zoo until dying in 1963.

segments.title: Bumps the St. Bernard with the Royal Norwegian Navy
segments.summary: Bumps, a St. Bernard, was adopted by the Royal Norwegian Navy with Lieutenant Erling Haftorn on the Thorodd. The dog served in Scotland, helped with rescues and foiled a mugging, rode buses, and was honored with a posthumous PDSA Gold Medal in 2006.

segments.title: Listener mail on MH370 episode
segments.summary: A listener from Kuala Lumpur praises the MH370 episode and comments on Malaysian cultural attitudes toward fate. The hosts thank him and give contact information.
